Q: can 7zZip compress non encrypting and without random salt? A:

7-Zip no usa sal aleatoria cuando no hay cifrado. Si comprimes archivos sin activar el cifrado, no existe ningún proceso criptográfico que cambie el resultado. La razón por la que los archivos .7z cambian aunque el contenido sea igual es porque el archivo comprimido guarda metadatos, como fechas de modificación, acceso o creación, y a veces el orden de los archivos dentro del contenedor. Esos datos pueden variar cada vez que se crea el archivo, produciendo un hash diferente. Para reducir esto, puedes desactivar los timestamps con -mtc=off -mtm=off -mta=off o usar tar para crear un archivo determinista antes de comprimirlo con 7-Zip.

Q: What to do when you want to split column but your dataframe was fused and transposed, and that column is now an index? A:

I made minimal working code with example data directly in code (I used io.StringIO() to simulate file) - so everyone can simply copy and run it.

import pandas as pd
import io


text = """        aac(6')=HMM  aac(6')-I=COMPETE  aac(6')-Ib-cr5=COMPLETE  aac(6')-Ie/aph(2'')-Ia=COMPLETE
the_meat ; ; ;1687  0   0   0   0
the_meat ;chicken ; ;205    0   0   0   0
the_meat ;chicken ;cajan chicken salad ;1   0   0   0   0
"""

df = pd.read_csv(io.StringIO(text), sep=r"\s{2,}", engine="python")
df = df.reset_index()


print("\n--- after read_csv() and reset_index() ---")
print(df)

df["index"] = df["index"].str.split(";")

print('\n--- after df["index"].str.split(";") ---')
print(df)

df[["Type", "Subtype", "Sub-subtype", "N"]] = df["index"].apply(pd.Series)
df = df.drop(columns=["index"])

print('\n--- after df["index"].apply(pd.Series) --- new columns are at the end ---')
print(df)

# fmt: off
df = df[ ["Type", "Subtype", "Sub-subtype", "N", "aac(6')=HMM", "aac(6')-I=COMPETE", "aac(6')-Ib-cr5=COMPLETE", "aac(6')-Ie/aph(2'')-Ia=COMPLETE"] ]
# fmt: on

print("\n--- after changing order ---")
print(df)

EDIT: little shorter version

df = pd.read_csv(io.StringIO(text), sep=r"\s{2,}", engine="python")
df = df.reset_index()

print("\n--- after read_csv() and reset_index() ---")
print(df)

new_columns = df["index"].str.split(";").apply(pd.Series)
df = df.drop(columns=["index"])

df.insert(0, "Type", new_columns[0])
df.insert(1, "Suptype", new_columns[1])
df.insert(2, "Sub-subtype", new_columns[2])
df.insert(3, "N", new_columns[3])

print('\n--- after df["index"].str.split(";").apply(pd.Series) and .insert() ---')
print(df)

Q: Getting StopIteration when using HuggingFaceEndpoint with LangChain and flan-t5-large A:

This error occurs when Hugging Face can’t find any Inference Provider that can serve the model you selected so the provider list is empty and the client raises StopIteration.

The fix would be to use models that have an Inference Provider available on Hugging Face (or deploy the model as your own Inference Endpoint). You can find provider-supported models on the Hugging Face Models page by using the Inference available filter (see screenshot below)

Q: Enterprise patterns for VS Code extension governance A:

Having a whitelist of the vendor companies is not a bad idea. But it should not touch such a field as the computers of the developers and the installed software, not even to mention open-source extensions.

The approach should be different and simple. Developer's computers should be isolated from the corporate network. The communication should circulate only documents, source code, and similar safe matter.

From what I can see in your comments, I feel that your company is generally lost. Too bad...

By the way, in terms of security... Nothing is as dangerous as seeing a security risk in some safe stuff. It means the qualification and cognitive skills of the security specialists are so low that they simply loudly invite attackers while having no power to withstand real attacks.
